purpose: Player names, group names, OCR text and other text that reaches a CSV or XLSX export must stay text when the file is opened in a spreadsheet program. The real value stays unchanged in the database and the domain; only the export boundary changes it, and every import of these files undoes exactly that change.
xlsx: Write text as a string cell (shared or inline string, never a formula cell) and numbers as number cells. Do not add the CSV prefix in XLSX.

needsPrefix: A plain number never needs the prefix: an optional + or -, ASCII digits, optionally one . or , followed by ASCII digits (-5, +3, 12,5).
The first character is a control character U+0000-U+001F (tab, carriage return, line feed, ...).
After any leading spaces (U+0020, U+00A0, U+3000) the first character is one of = + - @ or their full-width forms U+FF1D U+FF0B U+FF0D U+FF20.
The value starts with ' and the rest needs the prefix (so a real leading apostrophe survives the round trip).
csv.export: Prefix the value with one ' when it needs the prefix; otherwise write it unchanged. Delimiter quoting is applied afterwards, as before.
csv.import: When a value starts with ' and the rest needs the prefix, drop exactly that one '; otherwise keep the value unchanged.
